_comment: This is the MAIN ENCYCLOPEDIA — the full definition of Account Takeover (ATO) and all its variants.
_comment2: Person 1 owns this file. Other team members READ from it but never modify it.

attack_objective._comment: WHAT does the attacker want to achieve?
attack_objective.summary: Gain unauthorized control of a legitimate user's payment account to perform fraudulent transactions
details: Access the victim's account using stolen or compromised credentials
Modify account settings (email, phone, address) to maintain control
Initiate unauthorized fund transfers to attacker-controlled beneficiaries
Exploit stored payment methods for fraudulent purchases

preconditions._comment: WHAT must be true BEFORE this attack can happen?
preconditions.summary: The attacker must have obtained valid account credentials through an external method
required: Attacker possesses valid login credentials (username + password)
Target account has active payment capability (linked bank account or card)
Target account is not currently locked or suspended
common_credential_sources: Phishing emails/websites that trick users into entering credentials
Data breaches where credentials were leaked from other services
Credential stuffing (trying leaked passwords from other sites)
Social engineering (calling the victim and tricking them)
Malware/keyloggers installed on the victim's device

observable_behaviour._comment: WHAT does this attack LOOK LIKE when it is happening? These are the patterns we watch for.
observable_behaviour.summary: Post-compromise activity patterns that differ from the legitimate account holder's normal behaviour

indicators.indicator: Login from unrecognized device or browser fingerprint
Login from a geographic location inconsistent with account history
Immediate payment to a never-before-seen beneficiary after login
Transaction amount significantly outside normal spending pattern
Rapid sequence of transactions in short time window
Activity at unusual hours for this account holder

payment_consequences.summary: Unauthorized fund transfers leading to direct financial loss for the account holder
consequences: Funds transferred to attacker-controlled bank accounts
Unauthorized purchases using stored payment cards
Account balance drained through multiple smaller transactions
Chargeback costs and dispute resolution expenses for the institution

genai_enhancement._comment: HOW does Generative AI make this attack MORE dangerous?
genai_enhancement.summary: GenAI enables attackers to scale and improve the quality of ATO attacks

enhancements.description: GenAI creates highly convincing, personalized phishing emails that bypass spam filters and fool users
enhancements.impact: Increases credential theft success rate by 3-5x

enhancements.description: AI clones the victim's voice to bypass phone-based verification or trick bank support staff
enhancements.impact: Defeats voice-based authentication and social verification

enhancements.description: AI optimizes credential stuffing by learning which password variations are most likely to work
enhancements.impact: Reduces time to compromise from hours to minutes

enhancements.description: AI studies the legitimate user's transaction patterns and mimics them to avoid detection
enhancements.impact: Makes post-compromise activity harder to distinguish from legitimate use

simulation_parameters.description: Whether the simulated transaction comes from a new device
Whether the simulated transaction comes from a new location
Whether the payment goes to a never-before-seen beneficiary
How much the amount deviates from normal (0.0 = normal, 1.0 = max deviation)
How much the transaction speed deviates from normal (0.0 = normal, 1.0 = max deviation)
Whether the transaction occurs at an unusual time

detection_signals._comment: These are the specific red flags the detection system should watch for

primary_signals.description: High-confidence indicator — most ATO attacks come from a device the account never used before
High-confidence indicator — attackers send money to accounts they control

secondary_signals.description: Medium-confidence — depends on how far from normal
Medium-confidence — rapid transactions are suspicious but not conclusive

weak_signals.description: Low-confidence alone — people sometimes transact at odd hours

variants.name: High-Value New Device Takeover
variants.description: Classic high-risk ATO: attacker logs in from an unknown device, sends a large payment to a new beneficiary. Easiest to detect but also the most damaging if missed.
variants.notes: This is the 'textbook' ATO. If the system cannot detect this, something is fundamentally wrong.

variants.name: Velocity Burst from Known Device
variants.description: Attacker uses a device the victim has used before (e.g., compromised via malware). Sends multiple rapid payments to new beneficiaries. The known device makes it trickier.
variants.notes: The known device removes a major signal. Detection must rely on velocity + new beneficiary combination.

variants.name: Off-Hours Location Shift
variants.description: Attacker logs in from a new location at an unusual time but keeps transaction amounts normal. Tries to fly under the radar by not being greedy.
variants.notes: Could be legitimate travel. The combination of new location + unusual time is the key signal here.

variants.name: Subtle Amount Deviation (Stealth Mode)
variants.description: The sneakiest variant. Attacker uses a known device, pays a known beneficiary, but slightly increases the amount. Almost indistinguishable from legitimate activity.
variants.notes: This is the hardest variant to detect. Only subtle amount deviation gives it away. Tests the system's sensitivity to small changes.

variants.name: Multi-Signal Low-Intensity
variants.description: Multiple signals fire but all at low intensity. No single signal is alarming on its own, but the combination should raise suspicion. Tests the system's ability to correlate weak signals.
variants.notes: The key test: can the system detect fraud when many small anomalies combine? No single red flag, but the pattern is suspicious.

attack_objective.summary: Rapidly exfiltrate, layer, and cash out stolen or illicit funds through multi-hop mule account rings
details: Launder funds across multiple intermediary accounts to obscure transaction origin
Structure transactions into micro-transfers to evade CTR / AML reporting thresholds
Consolidate multiple mule accounts into a single master cash-out wallet or crypto off-ramp
Exploit dormant aged accounts as high-trust intermediaries

preconditions.summary: Attacker controls compromised source funds or mule network accounts
required: Access to compromised accounts (via ATO) or mule recruits
Active P2P, ACH, or wire payment rails
Mule accounts prepared with cash-out channels
common_credential_sources: Synthetic identities created for credit/mule exploitation
Bought credentials on dark web forums

observable_behaviour.summary: High-velocity multi-hop graph flows with minimal account balance retention

indicators.indicator: Rapid outflow of funds within minutes of receipt
One account sending to 10+ distinct receivers in short window
Multiple accounts sending to 1 central consolidation account
Transfers structured just below $10,000 threshold
Multiple sender/receiver accounts sharing identical device or IP subnet
Zero-history dormant account suddenly routing large volumes

payment_consequences.summary: Irreversible fund loss as money is funneled to unrecoverable cash-out endpoints
consequences: Permanent loss of victim funds through crypto/cash off-ramps
Regulatory fines for financial institutions failing to detect AML smurfing
Secondary account compromise across innocent mule victims

genai_enhancement.summary: Autonomous GenAI agents orchestrating adaptive money movement networks

enhancements.description: GenAI dynamically selects mule accounts with the lowest risk scores to route funds
AI models legitimate cardholder habits and spreads micro-transfers across days to evade time-window alerts
enhancements.impact: Blends illicit transfers with natural commerce

simulation_parameters.description: How fast funds are forwarded (0.0=slow, 1.0=instant transit)
Whether mule nodes share device/IP hardware

primary_signals.description: Near-zero transit time between in-flow and out-flow
Hardware or IP sharing across multi-account transfers

secondary_signals.description: Rapid smurfing split across multiple destination nodes
Funneling of multiple transfers into single aggregator
High passthrough ratio with minimal account balance retention

weak_signals.description: Sudden activity after long dormancy period

variants.name: Rapid Cash-Out Burst
variants.description: Immediate high-velocity outflow: stolen funds are wired or cashed out within seconds of arriving at destination.
variants.notes: Classic rapid drain. Velocity and shared device make it an immediate critical block.

variants.name: Smurfing / Layered Fan-Out
variants.description: Attacker splits $10,000+ stolen lump sums into 10-15 micro-transfers to distinct mule accounts to bypass single-transaction AML limits.
variants.notes: Smurfing relies on graph fan-out anomaly detection to catch the dispersal phase.

variants.name: Fan-In Consolidation Ring
variants.description: Multiple intermediate mule accounts funnel their micro-balances into a single aggregator wallet or crypto off-ramp.
variants.notes: Aggregation endpoint detection using in-degree centrality and shared IP/device clusters.

variants.name: Dormant Mule Ring Activation
variants.description: Aged bank accounts that sat dormant for 6+ months suddenly wake up and route high-value layered transfers.
variants.notes: High trust history makes detection difficult; dormancy anomaly + passthrough ratio triggers Step-Up.

attack_objective.summary: Deploy autonomous Generative AI agents, synthetic biometrics, and adversarial evasion to bypass payment defenses
details: Automate hyper-personalized spear phishing and conversational social engineering via LLM agents
Synthesize realistic voice/video deepfakes to authorize high-value executive wire transfers
Generate synthetic identities with valid MRZ checksums and AI portraits to bypass KYC onboarding
Apply gradient-free adversarial perturbations to transaction attributes to evade fraud classifiers

preconditions.summary: Attacker possesses LLM API access, voice synthesis models, or diffusion-based ID generators
required: Access to generative voice/image/text AI models
Target organizational hierarchy / vendor relationship data
Target payment gateway API or customer support interaction channel
common_credential_sources: Public executive audio (podcasts, earnings calls, conferences)
OSINT data from LinkedIn and company directories
Stolen SSN fragments combined with diffusion-generated faces

observable_behaviour.summary: Anomalous linguistic urgency, synthetic biometric acoustic flatness, and near-threshold amount clustering

indicators.indicator: High semantic urgency score in communication channel
Lack of natural acoustic micro-tremors in voice verification
Synthetic facial embedding lack of sub-surface skin scattering
Transactions repeatedly clustering just below risk boundary ($1,999 vs $2,000)

payment_consequences.summary: Direct unauthorized high-value wires and maxed-out synthetic credit lines
consequences: Multi-million dollar corporate wire loss via executive deepfake authorization
Credit line write-offs on synthetic identity accounts

genai_enhancement.summary: AI is the core engine of the attack itself rather than just a helper tool

enhancements.description: Clones CFO voice with under 5s of audio to authorize same-day wires
Optimizes payment features to minimize classifier score while maximizing extracted cash

primary_signals.description: Lack of natural acoustic jitter in voice authorization
Diffusion artifact detection in KYC facial scan

secondary_signals.description: High semantic pressure and urgency Framing
Near-threshold clustering and systematic evasion patterns

variants.name: Conversational Fraud Agent
variants.description: Autonomous LLM bot ingesting victim social feeds to execute real-time conversational social engineering on support channels.
variants.notes: NLP intent modeling detects prompt injection and coercion heuristics.

variants.name: Deepfake Voice / Video Authorization
variants.description: Attacker clones CFO/vendor voice to call treasury and push an urgent high-value wire authorization.
variants.notes: Acoustic micro-tremor and acoustic environment jitter reveal synthetic speech generation.

variants.name: Synthetic Identity (GenAI KYC Bypass)
variants.description: AI combines real SSN fragments with diffusion-generated portraits and synthetic credit histories.
variants.notes: Sub-surface skin scattering and synthetic embedding distance flags fabricated profiles.

variants.name: Adaptive Adversarial Feature Evasion
variants.description: Black-box optimizer tweaks payment features (amounts just below threshold, off-hour timing) to evade fraud detectors.
variants.notes: Adversarial boundary entropy tracking catches deliberate score perturbation.

details: AI spear phishing
CEO/vendor voice cloning
Urgent payment pretexting

observable_behaviour.summary: High conversational urgency, new destination accounts with familiar beneficiary names

Voice acoustic jitter anomaly

Manipulate currency/amount fields in API payloads

API parameter mutation
Merchant geo-location mismatch
